```python

```

If `router` is `self`, then `self.routes` is iterated. `self.add_api_route` adds a route to `self.routes`.
This IS an infinite loop if `self.routes` is not a static list.
In Python, if you iterate over a list and append to it, you get an infinite loop.

So `if router is self:` is exactly the right fix for this.

`router_a.include_router(router_b)`: `router_a` now has all routes of `router_b` (which includes routes of `router_a`).
This just duplicates routes, it doesn't cause an infinite loop during `include_router` call itself, because `router_b.routes` is already populated.
